```{r}
Students_Performance <- read.csv("StudentsPerformance.csv",stringsAsFactors = TRUE)

view(Students_Performance)
head(Students_Performance)



#Define Success so that around 15-20% or so of students are successful
#Come up with your own, this is just an example
Students_Performance$Success <- factor(ifelse( Students_Performance$reading.score > 75 & Students_Performance$writing.score > 75 & Students_Performance$math.score > 75,"Yes","No" ) )
mean(Students_Performance$Success=="Yes")
# 18.8%


#Eliminate scores (they aren't known obviously before test is taken)
Students_Performance$math.score <- NULL
Students_Performance$reading.score <- NULL
Students_Performance$writing.score <- NULL
```

```{r}

#Make special datasets for examining partial dependence plots, interactions, and breakdown plots 
TRAIN.PREDICTORS <- Students_Performance
TRAIN.PREDICTORS$Success <- NULL
TRAIN.TARGET <- as.numeric(Students_Performance$Success=="Yes")

```


```{r}
#Estimating generalization error (build on a 70% training set and evaluate on a 30% holdout sample
#Normally this is done with K-fold crossvalidation and caret, but this is faster!
#Drawback:  only one guess of the generalization error! 
DATA <- Students_Performance
y <- "Success"
set.seed(479); train.rows <- sample(1:nrow(DATA),0.7*nrow(DATA))
MODEL <- randomForest(formula(paste(y,"~.")),data=DATA[train.rows,])
#Estimated accuracy on holdout sample (one measure of generalization error)
postResample(predict(MODEL,newdata=DATA[-train.rows,]),DATA[-train.rows,y] )
#Accuracy on holdout if predicted everything as the majority class (naive model)
max(table(DATA[-train.rows,y])/nrow(DATA[-train.rows,]))
#Estimated AUC on holdout sample (one measure of generalization error); 0.5 is random guessing, 1 is perfect
roc(DATA[-train.rows,y], predict(MODEL,newdata=DATA[-train.rows,],type="prob")[,2] )

```



```{r}
#Building an explainer with a random forest
library(randomForest)
FOREST <- randomForest(Success~.,data=Students_Performance)
summarize_tree(FOREST)
model_explainer <- DALEX::explain(FOREST, data = TRAIN.PREDICTORS,  y = TRAIN.TARGET)
model_vi <- model_parts(model_explainer, loss_function = loss_one_minus_auc)
plot(model_vi)
model_vi
```

```{r}
model_explainer$data$parental.level.of.education <- factor(
  model_explainer$data$parental.level.of.education,
  levels = c("some high school", "high school", "some college", "associate's degree", "bachelor's degree", "master's degree")  # Desired order
)

```


```{r}
FOREST <- randomForest(Success ~ ., data = Students_Performance)

# Summarize the model structure (optional, for deeper understanding)
# summarize_tree(FOREST) # Uncomment if you have this function available

# Create the explainer with added customization for label and color
model_explainer <- DALEX::explain(
  FOREST,
  data = TRAIN.PREDICTORS,
  y = TRAIN.TARGET,
  label = "RANDOM"
)

# Compute variable importance with customization (top 10 variables, AUC loss function)
model_vi <- model_parts(model_explainer, loss_function = loss_one_minus_auc)

# Print a summary of the variable importance
summary(model_vi)

# Plot the variable importance with custom titles and theme
# Plot with custom title and gray background, removing the default label
vi_plot <- plot(model_vi) +
  ggtitle("Top 10 Feature Importances - Random Forest Model (AUC)") +  # Custom title
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Features", y = "Contribution to Model's Accuracy") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#4CAF50", "#FFC107", "#F44336")) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",         # Removes the legend
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90", color = NA), # Gray plot background
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90", color = NA), # Gray panel background
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray80"),            # Light gray grid lines
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),                            # No minor grid lines
   
  )




# Display the plot
print(vi_plot)

# Display variable importance data if needed
model_vi







```

```{r}
#Breakdown plot showing how particular prediction is pieced together
#Choose two types of rows that tell a good story
predictions <- predict(FOREST,type="prob")[,2] #Get predicted probability of each row
which(predictions >= quantile(predictions,.99))  #Some of the rows with highest probabilities
which(predictions >= quantile(predictions,.49) & predictions <= quantile(predictions,.51))  #Some of the rows with typical value of y
which(predictions <= quantile(predictions,.01))  #Some of the rows with highest y
specific.row <- Students_Performance[111,]  
#The predict_parts can take a long time for big datasets doing classifications
plot( predict_parts(explainer = model_explainer, new_observation = specific.row, type = "break_down") )
```
```{r}
# Step 1: Get predictions from the random forest model
predictions <- predict(FOREST, type = "prob")[, 2]  # Get predicted probabilities for the positive class

# Step 2: Identify rows of interest based on quantiles
high_prob_index <- which(predictions >= quantile(predictions, 0.99))[1]  # Row with high predicted probability (top 1%)
low_prob_index <- which(predictions <= quantile(predictions, 0.01))[1]   # Row with low predicted probability (bottom 1%)

# Step 3: Extract the selected rows from the dataset
high_prob_row <- Students_Performance[high_prob_index, ]
low_prob_row <- Students_Performance[low_prob_index, ]

# Step 4: Generate breakdown plots for the selected rows

# Breakdown plot for the high probability row
high_prob_breakdown <- predict_parts(
  explainer = model_explainer, 
  new_observation = high_prob_row, 
  type = "break_down"
)

# Breakdown plot for the low probability row
low_prob_breakdown <- predict_parts(
  explainer = model_explainer, 
  new_observation = low_prob_row, 
  type = "break_down"
)

# Plot for high probability row
high_prob_plot <- plot(high_prob_breakdown) +
  theme_minimal() +  # Clean minimal theme
  theme(
    legend.position = "NULL",         
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90", color = NA), # Gray plot background
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90", color = NA), # Gray panel background
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray80"),            # Light gray grid lines
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14),  # Center and resize the title
    plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 10, 20),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 20)), 
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 5)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 15), size = 8),# Adjust the plot margins (top, right, bottom, left)

  
  ) + 
  labs(
    title = "Breakdown of Factors Leading to High Success Prediction", 
    x = "Parental Level of Education", 
    #find more info on what this actually represents
    y = "Average"
  )


# Plot for low probability row
low_prob_plot <- plot(low_prob_breakdown) +
  theme_minimal() +  # Clean minimal theme
  theme(
    legend.position = "NULL",         
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90", color = NA), # Gray plot background
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90", color = NA), # Gray panel background
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray80"),            # Light gray grid lines
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14),  # Center and resize the title
    plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 10, 20),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 20)), 
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 5)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 15), size = 8),# Adjust the plot margins (top, right, bottom, left)

  
  ) + 
  labs(
    title = "Breakdown of Factors Leading to Low Success Prediction", 
    x = "Parental Level of Education", 
    #find more info on what this actually represents
    y = "Average"
  ) 


# Display the plots
print(high_prob_plot)
print(low_prob_plot)
```
